title: Who else could extract for Duke
summary: They discuss the few people able to extract Duke's scores; Rose says people asked Juan how Duke did it and he would not tell, even for a blank check.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: But were there very, very few people who did this or could do this for him? There were maybe -- in all, maybe five people who did this, right?
Not five, I don't think.
Well, there was John Sanders -- didn't he do some when he was with the band?
You mean Father Sanders, who is a priest now?
Uh huh, Father Sanders.
I don't think so ...
I thought he did.
What?
John Sanders -- didn't he do some of this, too, some extracting?
Well, I don't know if he did or not; I don't know because I was not there when John Sanders at first, was in the band.
And Joe Benjamin did some, I think, and Herbie Jones. I think that's about all. Did Jimmie
Jones do any? Jimmie Jones?
Yeah ...
I don't know.
When you weren't there, I think -- but that's about all that ever worked on Duke's music.
Very few people could.
Yeah, that's what they say. In fact, some ...
Because I know a lot of people used to ask Juan, give me a hint how he does it, you know. And Juan said, 'Man, I can't do that.'

Oh, a lot of people. I had a Canadian fellow one time offer me -- he said, 'I write out a check and you put the amount in -- if you tell me how Duke does this and the other.' I said, 'Oh no, I can't do that. No.'
All the bands he went with, they would ask him the same question.
